questions.q: Put the real promotion steps in order, starting from a Completed Update Set on the source instance.
options: Retrieve, Export, Commit, Preview
Commit, Preview, Retrieve, Export
Preview, Export, Commit, Retrieve
Export, Retrieve, Preview, Commit
questions.explain: Export from the source, retrieve onto the target, preview the comparison, then commit to actually apply the changes.

options: The version of each change in the Update Set against the version currently on the target instance
The Update Set's file size against a maximum limit
The number of users logged into the source instance
The target instance's uptime against its SLA
questions.explain: Preview flags potential collisions by comparing the Update Set's version of each change against what currently exists on the target.

questions.q: Why is committing an Update Set straight from Dev to Production, skipping Test, considered a mistake even if Preview shows no flagged issues?
options: Because it defeats the purpose of a tracked, reviewable promotion path and removes the low-cost environment meant to catch problems
Because Preview cannot run on a Production instance at all
Because Production instances reject Update Sets by default
Because Test is required by ServiceNow's licensing terms
questions.explain: Test exists to catch exactly the kind of problem Preview flags, in an environment where a mistake costs nothing -- skipping it removes that safety net.

questions.q: What does 'Retrieve' actually do on the target instance?
options: Permanently deletes the Update Set from the source instance
Converts the Update Set into a Business Rule
Uploads/loads the exported XML file, creating a new, not-yet-applied Update Set record on the target
Immediately applies all captured changes without review
questions.explain: Retrieve brings the Update Set onto the target instance as a record ready for Preview -- it does not apply anything yet.

questions.q: What is the modern alternative to the manual export/retrieve/preview/commit cycle mentioned in this lesson?
options: Update Set batches and Source Control/DevOps integration, storing configuration as code and promoting via pipelines
There is no modern alternative; this cycle is the only method that has ever existed
Deleting Update Sets entirely and editing Production directly
Emailing the XML file to another administrator
questions.explain: Many organizations now use batches or DevOps/Source Control pipelines -- covered in depth in the later DevOps, Testing & Deployment course.
